feature: lobby sub-panel input gate — move/click while wedged, read-only RPM (also conditions 7/8)
supersedes: condition-2-lobby-panel-gate-rpm-verification.json (its 'modal input-owner state' conclusion is narrowed: the 0x100 cells are a button latch cleared by the next DOWN, not a dispatcher gate)
method: States: C1 responsive lobby; C2 環境設定 open (wedged); C3 wedged + VNC pointer move to (600,300) with no button; C4 wedged + one VNC click at (600,300) on the panel's empty area. Each state dumped 64 KB at 0x02210000 via OpenProcess(PROCESS_VM_READ|PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION). No writes, no threads, no debugger, no input retries.
conclusion: Mouse delivery is alive while the lobby panel is wedged: the cursor cells follow a pure move and a click is recorded as a complete new press at its point. The +0x194/+0x294 value 0x100 is the panel-opening press left logically down (a bare LEFTUP does not clear it; the next DOWN does). The wedge is therefore not an input-owner/modal state and not transport loss. Remaining candidates: (a) panel controls are routed by the sub-panel selector 0x02216C80=1 to a manager whose hit-test never matches, or (b) the first click after opening is consumed clearing the latch and only the second click reaches controls. Decisive next live check (one sealed run): open panel -> one click on empty area -> one click on a control (閉じる/OK) -> capture + dump.
